findings.evidence: grep: lines 385, 400, 528 all read `have hik : i = Fin.addNat k 24 := by ext; simp [k]; omega`.
findings.fix: Use `Fin.ext (by simp only [Fin.val_addNat]; omega)` (or `by omega` after zeta-reducing `k`) so no unconstrained simp set sits between the two tactics; apply at all three sites.
findings.issue: `have hik : i = Fin.addNat k 24 := by ext; simp [k]; omega` uses a non-terminal full `simp` whose output `omega` must consume; if `simp` ever closes the goal or leaves a different shape, the proof breaks. Same line verbatim at 400 and 528.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Dual.lean:48-52 declares `dotProductEquiv` with `backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false` and `@[simps]`, generating `dotProductEquiv_apply_apply`, which lines 420 and 425 of this file already invoke.
findings.fix: Prove both with the explicit lemma the file already uses at lines 420/425: `by simp [dotProductEquiv_apply_apply]` (plus `RootPairing.pairing` unfolding for 441), reserving `(rfl)` for the genuine field projections at 429/433.
findings.issue: `f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum_toLinearMap_apply` (437) and `f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum_pairing` (441) are proved by bare `(rfl)`, which holds only by unfolding `LinearEquiv.toLinearMap`, the `Module.Dual` coercion and `dotProductEquiv`'s anonymous-constructor body — undocumented defeq across wrappers, on a definition Mathlib itself elaborates under `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false`.

findings.evidence: Lines 312-336 and 341-365 are 24 successive `refine Fin.cases (f4ReflectionIndex_…_N j) (fun i => ?_) i` steps closed by `fin_cases i; exact …_23 j`; no comment anywhere in 160-365 explains the structure.

findings.issue: The 48 single-index reflection lemmas (163-307) are glued by two 24-step nested `Fin.cases` chains (309-365) with no comment saying why the verification cannot be a single `decide +revert` over both indices; a reader cannot tell whether the explosion is a heartbeat necessity or accidental. The chains also silently depend on `Fin.castAdd 24 (Fin.succ^n 0)` being defeq to the `Fin 48` numeral, and an off-by-one in the chain is invisible.

findings.issue: `span_f4Root_eq_top` and `span_f4Coroot_eq_top` duplicate the same five-step argument with inconsistent internals (one introduces `S`/`hr`, the other inlines `subset_span`), and every leaf is closed by `simpa only using (… ▸ …)` — an empty simp set used to absorb defeq, which hides what the step actually needs.

summary: The table-driven `decide` skeleton is a reasonable choice, but the glue around it is brittle: non-terminal `simp` before `omega` in three places, `(rfl)` proofs that unfold `dotProductEquiv` through the `LinearEquiv` coercion when the explicit simp lemma is already used elsewhere in the file, verbatim-duplicated sub-proofs, and 240 lines of case-split boilerplate with no comment explaining why it must be written out.
